title: micro-case-studies-outcome-cards-v0
content:
Purpose
---
One-page micro case-studies meant to be clipped into deal playbooks and quick battlecards. Each card = 1 story + 3 metrics + a seller soundbite + quick objection response + recommended configuration (hosted/dedicated/private). Keep these short so reps can paste into emails or slide footers.

How to use
---
- Seller: drop the matching micro-card into your pitch for the persona (e.g., platform engineer, head of support)
- SDR/BDR: quick email snippet in the 2nd follow-up
- SE: paste slide on the 2nd or 3rd technical call when economics/questions come up

Structure per card (target = 120–200 words)
---
1) One-line context (persona + workload)
2) Before -> After metrics (latency, per-token cost, throughput or error reduction)
3) What we changed (model variant + infra config + simple prompt tweak)
4) Concrete seller soundbite (1 sentence)
5) Common objections + 1-liner replies
6) Quick CTA / next step for buyer (pilot ask)

Micro-card A: Retail search + assistant (pilot)
---
Context: Mid-market ecommerce chain (30 stores + web) wanted unified product QA + chat that reduces returns and search-related exits. Buyer persona: Head of Product / Platform.
Before: average search latency 1.2s; conversion from search results 2.1%; support deflection 6%
After (pilot): average generation latency 220ms (model split: small local reranker + hosted gen); search conversion up to 3.8% (+80% rel uplift); support deflection 19% (pilot routing + canned suggestions)
What we changed: put reranker on Dedicated small GPU pool (low-cost quantized model), hosted generation with prefix cache for FAQ-style responses, simple prompt template + 5 curated examples. Enabled prefix caching for repeated product queries.
Seller soundbite: "We cut your average search-to-purchase friction while shaving token cost by ~35% with a split rerank+generate flow."
Objections + replies:
- "We worry about integration work" -> "We ship a 2-week integration starter with Reference API templates and starter backend code — you’ll be able to run a pilot without heavy infra changes."
- "Latency matters for checkout" -> "We can pin reranker locally and keep gen on hosted with a 200ms p95 by batching + cache — measurable before deeper infra work."
CTA: 6-week pilot: Reranker on Dedicated + hosted gen; success metric = +2% conversion or >15% deflection.

Micro-card B: Legal QA summarization for enterprise KB
---
Context: Law firm + compliance team with 2M docs, need fast extractive summaries and citation trails for internal requests. Buyer persona: Head of Legal Ops / CTO.
Before: avg agent resolution time 3+ hours; manual research heavy; monthly cost of contracted legal research high
After (pilot): mean resolution time down to 18 minutes (first-draft), citation precision ~88% (manual verification reduced by ~50%), estimated >40% savings on external research costs in pilot cohort
What we changed: private deployment (VPC) with tuned open model (8-bit quantized) for on-prem-like compliance; retrieval-augmented generation with rerank + citation extractor; strict output schema enforced by function-calling and hallucination checks.
Seller soundbite: "Put the knowledge where your compliance controls live — faster answers, auditable citations, and clear cost savings compared to contractors."
Objections + replies:
- "We need data residency and KMS" -> "Private deployment with KMS/HSM integration, audit logs shipped with the pilot by default."
- "Accuracy concerns" -> "We enforce citation-first prompts + automated citation checks and include a manual verification cadence to gauge precision improvements."
CTA: Pilot with a 3-team proof-of-value (P0: private on VPC, success metric = mean resolution time <30 minutes + 80% citation precision).

Micro-card C: Support triage + intent routing (SaaS)
---
Context: B2B SaaS with 12K monthly customers; heavy incoming support queue; first-response time >6 hours; NPS suffering. Buyer persona: Head of Customer Support / CS Ops.
Before: avg first response 6–12 hours; 30% tickets escalated to engineers; CS headcount increasing quarter-over-quarter
After (pilot): first-response stable at <30 minutes (auto-triage + suggested replies), escalation rate down to 12%, synthetic agent replies handled 24% of tickets fully with follow-on human checks
What we changed: hosted inference for lightweight classification + suggested replies, dedicated path for high-risk customers (pinned lower-latency model); caching of frequent reply templates; integrated with Zendesk and pushed quick triage webhooks.
Seller soundbite: "Reduce time-to-first-response to minutes while keeping engineers focused on product fixes — this is how you scale support without doubling headcount."
Objections + replies:
- "We can’t allow auto-replies for legal/regulatory tickets" -> "We scope auto-reply to low-risk categories and route flagged items to human queue; we provide audit logs for every message."
CTA: 30-day pilot scoped to 5K monthly tickets: success = first-response <1hr for 80% of tickets and escalation <15%.

Seller cheat snippets (copy-paste)
---
1) Email 2nd follow-up (search pilot): "Quick note — we recently ran a 6-week pilot for a retailer and improved search conversion by +80% while reducing token cost ~35%. Can we schedule a 20-min tech discovery to map your top search flows?"
2) Tech call opener (legal KB): "If your team is evaluating private deployments for sensitive KBs, we can show a working pilot with KMS + auditable citations in under 3 weeks."
3) Objection zinger (cost): "Start with a narrow pilot and measurable KPIs — our tooling will show per-ticket/per-conversation economics within the pilot window."

Deck/snippet ideas to build from these cards
---
- 1-slide micro-case with before/after metrics + 2 visual ticks showing config (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- 2-slide seller insert (card + 1-liner script + CTA)
- Quick 1-minute demo script for SEs that shows latency and cost numbers live

Notes to self (rough)
---
- Keep micro-cards under 200 words; compress metrics to two lines if needed
- Prioritize cards for platform-engineer and head-of-support personas first
- When packaging for AE deck, include a tiny architecture callout: "what runs where" (1 sentence)
- Consider email A/B testing on the 2 follow-ups to measure open->demo conversion
